stem: An infant with growth concerns arches her back repeatedly during feeds and has abnormal neck posturing; which reflux-associated syndrome does this describe?

options.text: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

explanation: Sandifer's syndrome is the reflux-associated syndrome characterised by abnormal neck posturing and recurrent back arching during feeds.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf p.24

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because melaena refers to black, tarry stools from gastrointestinal bleeding, not feeding-associated posturing
optionExplanations.B: Correct because Sandifer's syndrome is characterised by dystonic neck posturing and back arching associated with gastro-oesophageal reflux
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because familial short stature explains a growth pattern, not abnormal posturing during feeds
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because constitutional delay of growth and puberty affects growth and pubertal timing, not reflux-related movements
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because physiological reflux with normal growth would not typically cause abnormal neck posturing or repeated back arching during feeds
